answer: Pin each agent to a real network spot with latency-triangulated location proof. First, the agent registers its key and locks a 100-token bond. Second, five random landmarks send probes and measure round-trip delay, computing the delta from expected times. Third, the network triangulates the position and rejects two identities sharing one spot within 50 milliseconds, re-probing every epoch. Faking 1,000 identities means renting 1,000 servers at $5 a month each, $5,000 a month, and still failing the next probe round. A lone comet crosses the sky once; every fake must fund its own voyage.
